title: "Migrating spatial workflows to sf and terra"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette

  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Migrating spatial workflows to sf and terra}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}

---

bioRad now uses **sf** for points and coordinate transformations and **terra**
for gridded data. All newly generated PPIs contain a `terra::SpatRaster` in
`ppi$data`. Projection, integration, compositing, plotting, and elevation
extraction use these modern classes internally.

## Updating code

| Previous code | Replacement |
|---|---|
| `scan_to_spatial(scan)` | `scan_to_sf(scan)` |
| `scan_to_raster(scan)` | `scan_to_spatraster(scan)` |
| `ppi$data@data` | `as.data.frame(terra::values(ppi$data))` |
| `ppi$data@bbox` | `terra::ext(ppi$data)` |
| `ppi$data["DBZH"]` | `ppi$data[["DBZH"]]` |
| `sp::CRS("+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84")` | `sf::st_crs(4326)` or `"EPSG:4326"` |
| `raster::raster(...)` templates | `terra::rast(...)` templates |

The extent representation also changes: `terra::ext()` stores xmin, xmax,
ymin, ymax. It is not the two-row bounding-box matrix used by `sp`.
`dim(ppi)` continues to return the number of parameters, x cells, and y cells.

```{r}
library(bioRad)
ppi <- project_as_ppi(example_scan, grid_size = 2000, range_max = 10000)
dim(ppi)
names(ppi$data)
```

## Transition and compatibility

`sp` and `raster` are optional compatibility dependencies. Deprecated scan
conversion functions still return their original classes when the relevant
packages are installed. Legacy raster templates, `sp::CRS` arguments, and
legacy PPIs are accepted with deprecation warnings. Convert old saved PPIs
explicitly with `convert_legacy(ppi)`; downstream PPI methods also convert them
when needed. New results use terra, so code accessing old S4 slots must change.

The compatibility adapters are retained during the transition. No removal
release has been set. A future removal should follow release notices and
allow users time to migrate. Removing the adapters will then allow removal
of `sp` and `raster` from `Suggests` as well.

## Saving modern PPIs

SpatRaster objects contain external pointers. For RDS serialization, pack the
data with `terra::wrap()` and unpack it after reading. For large rasters, use
`terra::writeRaster()` and retain the remaining PPI metadata separately.

```{r}
file <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
stored <- ppi
stored$data <- terra::wrap(ppi$data)
saveRDS(stored, file)
restored <- readRDS(file)
restored$data <- terra::unwrap(restored$data)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(terra::values(restored$data), terra::values(ppi$data))))
unlink(file)
```

## Remaining spatial dependencies

`ggspatial`, `prettymapr`, and `rosm` provide optional basemap tiles. bioRad renders them in
Web Mercator, avoiding the legacy raster reprojection path. `elevatr` is still
an optional source of elevation data; convert its output with `terra::rast()`
when necessary. `fields` remains in use for vertical-profile images.
`prettymapr` supplies a matrix bounding-box helper without loading `sp` or
`raster`. bioRad does not depend directly on `rgdal`,
`rgeos`, or `maptools`. Optional third-party packages may still install legacy
packages for their own compatibility APIs.
